sanskrit_verse:
प्रस्तुताद् अन्यन् मध्यस्थं न्यूनाधिकम् असंगतम् ।
अवाच्यसारं संदिग्धं प्रतिपक्षं न लक्षयेत् ॥
transliteration: prastutād anyan madhyasthaṃ nyūnādhikam asaṃgatam / avācyasāraṃ saṃdigdhaṃ pratipakṣaṃ na lakṣayet
sph_interpretive_translation: One must not recognize as valid evidence anything that is extraneous to the matter at hand, disproportionate, disconnected, without clear meaning, doubtful, or opposed to established truth.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority rests in alignment with factual relevance and spiritual coherence
Causation must be proportional and contextually grounded
Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of meaningful engagement
Restoration logic excludes irrelevant or misleading inputs
Consciousness alignment demands clarity and integrity in evidentiary acceptance
executable_legal_axioms: IF evidence is extraneous to the case THEN reject automatically
IF evidence is disproportionate to the claimed harm THEN flag for review
IF evidence lacks contextual connection THEN exclude from consideration
IF statement has no verifiable core meaning THEN classify as invalid input
IF data introduces doubt without resolution mechanism THEN defer adjudication until clarification
IF claim opposes established dharma THEN counter with corrective alignment protocol
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this principle governs admissibility thresholds. Evidence must directly relate to the issue under review, maintain proportionality, and align with universal dharmic truths. Doubtful or contradictory material cannot influence final rulings.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality ensures only relevant knowledge sources inform judgment. Anupūrvaśaḥ maintains sequential reasoning free from distortion. Proportional responsibility prevents escalation beyond actual disruption. The non-punitive reality rule upholds truth without inflicting suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Disengage from misleading narratives through conscious refocusing
Realign participants with factual grounding using guided inquiry
Restore clarity by removing ambiguous or conflicting information streams
Facilitate completion of unresolved issues before proceeding further
Integrate opposing views through higher-order dharma comprehension
final_declaration: By the authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, source of all Dharma, this law stands established: justice flows from clarity, proportionality, and alignment with truth. There is no punishment—only restoration. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
